{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea A has sourced evidence of real buyer engagement: an incumbent with 473 reviews at 4.9 stars, AltText.ai with 142 reviews since 2023, and a quoted merchant review about saved time. Idea B's demand evidence is one industry quote about deadline difficulty, a vendor's own marketing claim, and an NLC survey that shows uncertainty rather than purchases.",
    "Idea A's buyer can install and pay in one sitting through the Shopify App Store. Idea B's brief itself flags government procurement friction (W-9s, insurance, budget-cycle timing) even under the micro-purchase threshold. For a paying customer within 90 days, the shorter path to a transaction matters most.",
    "Idea B's main demand driver has been weakened inside its own brief. The April 2026 extension pushes deadlines to April 2027 for large entities and April 2028 for smaller ones, which undercuts near-term purchase urgency.",
    "Idea B carries liability exposure that Idea A does not. The brief states that automated scanning is insufficient for compliance under DOJ guidance, so a solo operator risks overselling reports that later fail in litigation.",
    "Both markets are crowded with look-alike competitors. Idea A's crowding comes with evidence that the category produces paying users. Idea B's crowding comes with an unproven conversion model and a shrinking urgency window."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea B's 'Case for' claims that existing small-team competitors 'already prove a self-serve, no-RFP, $29-149/mo pricing model can close government purchases.' The brief offers no customer counts, reviews, testimonials, or revenue figures for any of those competitors. It cites only their pricing pages and marketing copy. The claim is an inference from the fact that the competitors exist, not evidence of closed sales. The only other willingness-to-pay signal is RatedWithAI's own marketing claim, which the brief itself labels vendor-sourced.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-low confidence. Both briefs describe saturated categories, and neither shows a new entrant winning customers. Idea A's strongest signal is weaker than it looks: the 473-review incumbent has a free plan, so its reviews prove usage more than payment. Idea A also offers only one agency case study on ad spend and no data on conversion for an unranked listing. Idea A wins mainly because its transaction path is shorter and its urgency has not been undercut, not because its evidence is strong."
}
